Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE...

Bangladesh Women will be happy too. The ball is coming nicely onto the bat apart from the odd balls. Their bowlers were decent. The spinners made a real impact but to avoid a clean sweep, their batters have to really step up. The top four has been doing so but not enough to cross the victory line. Can they do so today?

So, Bangladesh Women need 125 runs to win in 14 overs. A solid effort from India though to go full throttle one we had the resumption after the rain delay. Smriti Mandhana and Dayalan Hemalatha were batting well in the middle but we lost more than hour of play due to rain and that saw change in plans from India and they did well to hit a couple of overs for 10-15 runs.

It's time for the fourth match between India Women and Bangladesh Women. The series have already been clinched by the visitors as they have taken an unassailable lead of 3-0 but there is still a lot to play for in this series. Bangladesh Women definitely would love to churn something out of this series now as they are playing in front of their home crowd and wouldn't like a clean sweep. Also, the World Cup is just around the corner so there is still a lot of time for both teams to test their bench and try something different. Let's hope we get a cracking conntest. Stay tuned.
...Match Day...

The stage is set for yet another thrilling encounter as Bangladesh Women gear up to face India Women in the 4th T20I at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium. With India Women already securing the series with dominant performances in the first three games, Bangladesh Women find themselves in a tough situation and with a lot at stake, especially considering the T20 World Cup looming large on the horizon. India Women have been flawless throughout the series, and the last game was no exception. Led by Radha Yadav, the bowlers staged a remarkable comeback after Bangladesh's strong start. Spinners Deepti Sharma and Shreyanka Patil combined effectively to stem the flow of runs, keeping the Bangladesh batters at bay and restricting them to a modest total of 117 runs in their allotted 20 overs. On the batting front for Bangladesh Women, Dilara Akter provided a blazing start but failed to capitalize on it. Although skipper Nigar Sultana and Sobhana Mostary had a brief partnership, the rest of the batting lineup faltered, leading to a below-par score. In the chase, the Indian openers Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma laid a solid foundation with a formidable 91-run stand, almost sealing the game and the series. The middle order then efficiently wrapped up the proceedings, capitalizing on the strong start provided by the openers. With the ball, Bangladesh Women found themselves struggling due to the lack of runs to defend, as the strong Indian batting order capitalized on the opportunity. As the series heads into its final two games, Bangladesh Women will be aiming to regroup and put up a stronger fight against the visitors, while India Women will be eyeing a clean sweep to further bolster their dominance in the series. Can the Bangladesh Women turn things around and win this one? We shall soon find out.
